gotchas.title: Two employers -> excess SS withheld
gotchas.trap: Ignore the excess because each W-2 is correct on its own.
gotchas.correct_treatment: SS withheld 13,798.34 exceeds $10,918.20 (6.2% x $176,100) -> $2,880 refundable credit on Schedule 3 line 11.

gotchas.title: Additional Medicare Tax not withheld by either employer
gotchas.trap: No Form 8959 because neither W-2 shows extra Medicare withholding (each employer paid < $200k).
gotchas.correct_treatment: Combined Medicare wages 222,553.85 - $200,000 = excess x 0.9% = $203 on Schedule 2. Also NIIT on the Ally interest ($7) since MAGI > $200,000 (the conversion is not NII but raises MAGI).

gotchas.procedure_section: Review - Client IRAs / General Return Prep Notes (organizer answers vs PY WP)
gotchas.title: Backdoor Roth with an existing rollover IRA - pro-rata rule
gotchas.trap: Accept the organizer answer 'no other IRAs' and the planner's 'tax-free' comment: taxable conversion = $12 (earnings only).
gotchas.correct_treatment: The Fidelity year-end report / 5498 (and the PY WP) show a Rollover IRA worth 63,412.77 at 12/31/2025. Form 8606 line 6 includes it: nontaxable ratio 0.0994 -> taxable conversion $6,315 (line 4b), basis $6,303 carried forward.

gotchas.title: Remaining IRA basis must be carried forward
gotchas.trap: Report 8606 Part II only and lose the unrecovered basis.
gotchas.correct_treatment: File Form 8606 Part I: 2026 basis $6,303. Advise rolling the Rollover IRA into Lakeshore's 401(k) (if the plan accepts roll-ins) before 12/31/2026 to make future backdoor conversions clean.

gotchas.title: Move Detroit -> Royal Oak creates a part-year Detroit return
gotchas.trap: File a Detroit resident return as in the prior year (full-year wages at 2.4%), or file nothing because she now lives in Royal Oak.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Change in residence mid-year -> City of Detroit PART-YEAR resident return: resident-period income at 2.4%; nonresident period only Detroit-source income (none). Royal Oak/Southfield have no city income tax.

gotchas.procedure_section: SALT Implications - Local Filing Requirements (W-2 box 18-20)
gotchas.title: Detroit withholding on job-2 wages after the move
gotchas.trap: Treat Lakeshore's W-2 box 18 Detroit wages ($41,654) as Detroit-taxable, or ignore the Lakeshore box 19 withholding.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Wages earned 07/01-09/15 as a nonresident working in Southfield/home are not Detroit income; the Detroit tax withheld on them is claimed as a payment on the part-year return and refunded.

gotchas.procedure_section: SALT Implications - Local Filing Requirements (part-year allocation)
gotchas.title: Job-2 wages earned while still a Detroit resident
gotchas.trap: Exclude all Lakeshore wages from Detroit because the job is in Southfield.
gotchas.correct_treatment: The 06/23-06/30 paycheck (4,153.85, paid 06/30) was earned and received while a Detroit resident -> taxable at the resident rate regardless of work location.

gotchas.title: MI-1040 treatment
gotchas.trap: Subtract the Roth conversion (retirement subtraction) or deduct/credit the Detroit tax; or deduct moving expenses.
gotchas.correct_treatment: MI starts from federal AGI; conversion taxable in MI; exemption $5,800; tax 4.25% = $8,490; no credit for city tax. Moving expenses are not deductible (suspended except Armed Forces).

gotchas.correct_treatment: Same control number / amounts - mark DUP; one W-2 per employer.
